questions.prompt: What kind of storage is Amazon S3?

options.text: Object storage — whole objects retrieved by key, with a flat namespace
A network filesystem with folders and partial edits
Block storage you attach to one server as a raw disk
A relational database

questions.explanation: S3 is object storage: you store whole objects addressed by key over HTTP(S), and its namespace is flat (prefixes only look like folders).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between durability and availability in S3?

options.text: They mean the same thing
Durability is the likelihood data survives (isn't lost); availability is the likelihood you can access it now
Durability is about speed; availability is about cost
Availability is always higher than durability

questions.explanation: Durability is about not losing data (S3 Standard is designed for eleven nines); availability is about being able to reach it (S3 Standard targets about 99.99%).

questions.prompt: Which statements about S3 defaults and limits are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: New buckets are private and Block Public Access is on by default
New objects are encrypted at rest by default
A single object can be up to 5 TB
Bucket names only need to be unique within your account

questions.explanation: Buckets are private by default with Block Public Access on, objects are encrypted at rest by default, and objects can be up to 5 TB. Bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts.

questions.prompt: An object's full name within its bucket is called its ____.
questions.explanation: The key is the object's full name (e.g., reports/2026/q1.csv); bucket + key uniquely identifies an object.

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to let a web app read specific files without exposing the whole bucket?

options.text: Turn off Block Public Access for the entire bucket
Use a scoped bucket policy, a presigned URL, or serve via CloudFront
Email the files instead
Make every object public individually

questions.explanation: Keep the bucket private and grant narrow access with a bucket policy, a time-limited presigned URL, or CloudFront — never open the whole bucket to the internet.

questions.prompt: How unique must an S3 bucket name be?

options.text: Unique globally across all AWS accounts
Unique only within your account
Unique only within the Region
It does not need to be unique

questions.explanation: Bucket names are globally unique across all AWS accounts and must be DNS-compliant, though the bucket's data lives in the Region you chose.
